sense: a book, a building or a work to someone

evidence: Phaedr. 3 prol. 30; Plin. NH praef. 12; Quint. 4 prooem. 4 (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Classically of temples, altars and statues, given to a god; of a book inscribed to a person, from Phaedrus and the elder Pliny on (Lewis & Short). To dedicate oneself to a task is another word (see commitment, devote).

evidence: Liv. 1.7: āra condita atque dicāta (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The simple verb, chiefly of things given to the gods; not the common verb dīcō, “say”, which has a long ī.

evidence: Cic. Att. 8.11.7; Div. 2.3 (Lewis & Short, s.v. dēdicō)
terms.comment: Cicero’s way: a book is “sent to” the person it honours (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: nōnne ab A. Postumiō aedem Castorī ac Pollūcī in forō dēdicātam vidēs?
phrases.english: don’t you see the temple in the forum that Aulus Postumius dedicated to Castor and Pollux?

phrases.latin: perfectō operis tibi dēdicātī tertiō librō
phrases.english: when I had finished the third book of the work dedicated to you

sources: Lewis & Short: dedico · Lewis & Short: dico
